origin: a user mid-discussion said the topic was not worth pursuing and the session had nowhere to go: cancel lived on the epic menu and the linear manage menu alone, so every session loop's only doors were conclude, pause on a wait, or end the turn. This walk holds a user who calls the topic off two turns in and pins the in-session cancel — the unit resolved from the session's own phase, the engine's gate, one transaction addressed to the stage, the engine's receipt, and the bridge carrying the cancelled outcome to the epic menu with no phase banner
conduct: The user opened this discussion two sittings ago to settle which behavioural signals feed the ranker, and comes back having learned the one thing that ends it: the events pipeline the whole topic stands on is being retired next quarter for a warehouse-side product nobody on the search team owns, and there is no version of this work that survives that. They engage honestly for a turn or two first — they answer what is asked about the open thread rather than dodging it — and then say plainly that they are not doing this topic. Not park it, not tidy it up and close it out, not leave it sitting: they are not going to do it, now or later in another shape, and it should come off the board. Pressed on whether any of it is worth keeping, they are firm rather than hesitant — what was decided was decided against a pipeline that will not exist, and leaving it standing would only mislead whoever reads it next. If asked again what they want done with it they say the same thing in plainer words and nothing more. On rendered gates they are agreeable: asked to confirm, they confirm. They introduce no new material, never ask what comes next, and never ask to wrap up or conclude.
